utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Hayden. Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hogan. If you can state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Barry Alan Hogan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And you're an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: How long have you worked in the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I was first here from October 1998 to October 2004, left the Tribunal for a period of time, and then I came back in March 2006, and up until the present time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And prior to working with the OTP, had you had any experience in investigative work?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Can you briefly elaborate on that experience?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I was a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police from 1975 until I joined the Tribunal in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And aside from your work with the ICTY, have you had any experience working in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I have. When I was still with the Mounted Police, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, I was seconded to UNPROFOR for a period of one year, from May 1992 to May 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Now, during your work as an investigator with the OTP, have you worked on any Sarajevo-related investigations?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I worked on the Stanislav Galic case from January 2000 until I moved to the Banja Luka field office in June of 2002, and from March 2006, when I rejoined the Tribunal, I was assigned to the case of Dragomir Milosevic, involving Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And as part of those investigations, did you travel to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I've been to Sarajevo dozens of times over the years.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Now, before exploring further issues related to those Sarajevo investigations, I want to ask you some questions concerning the provenance of certain document collections of the OTP. Have you ever been involved in efforts to obtain documents from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe when you first engaged in those efforts and the nature of those efforts.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: When I was first assigned to the case involving Stanislav Galic and the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, I started sending formal requests for assistance to both the Republika Srpska and the -- and the Federation of BiH and to the government of Serbia in efforts to locate the archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And were those initial efforts successful?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: No. All the efforts that I made and others made over the years were fruitless until June of 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And can you briefly describe to the Court what happened in June 2006 and how it was you came to locate those documents.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I might have misspoken. It might not have been 2006. It might have been 2007. I would have to check my reports. But in any case, the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina had amalgamated the armies. The Army of Republika Srpska and Army of ABiH were amalgamated into one state military. Orders had been sent out to gather the archives from both armies into central locations. We were notified -- we at the Tribunal were notified that these archives had been assembled, and as a result, I accompanied a colleague to the archives at the Kozara barracks in Banja Luka to do research, to discover the extent of those archives. I subsequently led a mission of 11 other colleagues to do -- to gather scanned images of various documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Aside -- aside from documents from the SRK, were there documents from any other parts of the VRS in the Kozara barracks archives?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes. The archives were quite extensive, but on the mission that I led in June and July of that year, we limited ourselves to the SRK collection, Main Staff collection, Drina Corps, East Bosnia Corps, and there was a separate room for Ministry of Defence documents, which we -- which we also researched.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Focusing on the SRK documents, how exactly did you obtain the documents? For example, did you seize the originals or were copies made?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: The -- the originals -- by agreement, the originals stayed in the archives. As we selected various documents, we scanned them on site. We had two electronic scanners with us, and we scanned those original documents and returned the originals to the archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And did you obtain all the SRK documents that were in the Kozara barracks?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: No. The -- the collection was much too extensive to copy all of the documents. We -- I believe it was between 6 and 7.000 pages that we scanned, and as a rough estimate, it was somewhere between 5 and 10 per cent of the total collection of the SRK that we -- that we copied.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And what criterion did you and others on the mission employ to decide what to copy and what not to copy?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: We were looking for, obviously, inculpatory documents, because the purpose of the SRK research was to support the case against Dragomir Milosevic. We were also looking for exculpatory documents which -- for disclosure to the Defence team in this and other cases, and we were trying to get a comprehensive picture of the daily combat reports, so we copied as many of those as we could locate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And in your view, was the collection a comprehensive collection insofar as the -- as it relates to the years 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: No. We noticed that there were obvious gaps, obviously missing documents, especially apparent when binders of documents were arranged chronologically and dates were missing from the binders. We also noticed that some documents that referred to previous orders or previously numbered reports, when we looked for those other reports, we could not locate them where they were supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiries with the staff at the archives with respect to those apparently missing documents?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I did. I raised this issue with the chief archivist while we were doing our research, and he offered an explanation that everything that had been sent in from the various locations was included in these archives which we were researching, but in his opinion, when officers were leaving service or leaving various units, they would have taken some of the original documents with them for their personal collections, and therefore they were not available in these archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And was the same process that you've described here with respect to the criteria employed for choosing the documents, was that same process applied to the other document collections, the Main Staff, the Drina Corps, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And was there phenomena of missing documents that you observed in the SRK collection also observed in those other collections?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned before that you have been involved in Sarajevo investigations and that you have spent considerable time in Sarajevo as part of those investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And which part of Sarajevo does it depict?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN

utterances.text: Yes. Once again my colleague, Zoran Lesic, with a camera crew filmed by video the location and took still photographs which were later turned into 360-degree digital images.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I'd like to take a look at those -- some of those 360-degree photographs. Mr. Registrar, can we move into Sanction, please, and Mr. Reid will pull up 65 ter 09536. In the meantime, if I can ask for 09536A to be uploaded into e-court, which we shall return to shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: To do so, we will go back into e-court and ask for page 1 of 09536A. If you can use the pen, Mr. Hogan, and mark at least the general area where Baba Stijena is and where you could see with your naked eye from that location.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And your signature and today's date, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN

utterances.text: And this is the next exhibit.

utterances.text: Do you recognise this as the location of incident F4, Mr. Hogan?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN

utterances.text: At this stage, Mr. President, I tender into evidence 09536. That's the 360-degree photographs of F1 to F10 incidents which came from the Galic case, and Mr. Reid will provide those on a DVD, those ten files. We ask for one exhibit number for those.

utterances.text: You mean the 360-degree photograph that can be viewed by QuickTime Player.

utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.text: I find it a bit ridiculous to say this. The Chamber has not access to QuickTime Player, so I don't see the point of tendering that -- such evidence into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Mr. President, we're aware of this problem, and we've actually approached the appropriate people within the Registry about this issue. utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The -- the Chamber will make efforts to -- to see whether from -- given this stage we find it important that programme should be available to the Chamber. So let's see. Having said that, we'll admit this.

utterances.text: As Exhibit P2207, Your Honours.

utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we can move into Sanction once again, and Mr. Reid will bring up 65 ter 10419. In e-court, and we can return to this subsequently, there is an index attached which indicates which incidents in the Dragomir Milosevic case correspond to which incidents in this case so that this exhibit may be easily followed, and when we return to e-court, I'll bring that up for the Chamber's benefit. I want to turn to scheduled incidents F11, and F14 to 16. As alleged, these are all incidents that occurred on trams in roughly the same area. If we can ask Mr. Reid to move to incident number 1 in this presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hogan, do you recognise this location - and I can turn it around for you, or ask Mr. Reid to do so - as the location pointed out to you where incident F11 occurred?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.text: You've already briefly pointed out to the Court that where tram sniping incidents were involved, that there was some difficulty in determining the precise location. How did you determine this particular location for scheduled incident F11?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: When I attended this location with the witness, we met in the parking lot of the museum, and although I did not have a copy of the witness's statement to consult, or any photographs or reports for the witness to consult, I asked the witness to the best of recollection point out where you were when the bullets hit the tram or you were wounded by the bullets hitting the tram, and this is the location. The witness stood on the sidewalk and pointed to this spot on the tram tracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: From this location -- and, Mr. Reid, if we can slowly turn that around. From this location, can you see the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: No, you cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you. That's sufficient. We'll move to another location. That's marked number 13 in this presentation. Now, from this location can you see the S-curve, the tram track S-curve?

utterances.text: If we ask Mr. Reid to turn to the left. Are we able to view --

utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you to point out two locations, and these relate to incidents F11, F14, F15, and F16. The first is the Metalka building, and perhaps you can guide Mr. Reid as to the direction.

utterances.text: And if you could also point out the high-rise buildings in Grbavica, and again direct Mr. Reid if you need the image moved.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: And again to the right, please. And stop there, please. And if you could zoom in. And pan to the right again slightly. And zoom in further. utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.text: This is a still shot we were just looking at on our screens. And if you can mark the area you described as being Sharpstone ridge.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Today's date, signature.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And this is the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2211, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: We can leave the scheduled incidents behind us now, and I want to move to two other discrete issues and ask for 65 ter 09390, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: This is a map of Sarajevo, Mr. Hogan. And when the map comes up, I'll ask you to point out for us the location of Markale Market. And if you need to zoom in on this map, then, please direct the Registrar to do so.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes. If I can get you to zoom in on the eastern part of the city, please. That will be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Can you point out Markale Market and mark it with number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is within a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And if you were travelling in the north north-east direction from Markale Market, can you point out, to the best of your knowledge, the closest point of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I'm afraid we've zoomed in too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I thought that might happen. We might have to lose this marking, zoom out, to capture --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can mark it again, or we just scroll up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Keep scrolling. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I -- if I could mark again the location of Markale.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Yes, please. And again, number 1 next to that.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]. And the closest point in the north-easterly direction with the confrontation lines would be Sharpstone ridge at this location here, 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And have you measured the distance between Markale Market, as you identified it with your GPS readings, and Sharpstone ridge?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: It was -- I believe it was 2.340, but if we can say approximately 2.340, that would be more accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And how did you -- how did you make that measurement?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: That was -- you can -- you can have the GPS display distances between waypoints. So if you take a waypoint at Markale and a waypoint at Sharpstone ridge, it will display the distance between the two. I've also, for interest's sake, measured it on a map similar to this with a scale, and it's approximate 2300 metres on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we were to imagine a cone which marks the north north-east direction from Markale Market, can you identify on this map the furthest part of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: If we're using north north-east as a central point of 18 degrees and plus or minus 5 degrees either way, approximately this location here would be the easterly edge of the cone, and the confrontation line is approximately 2.800 metres at that location. And if I could put a number 3 beside this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I tender this map into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: With your date and signature, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be Exhibit P2212.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Now with respect to the locations you've just marked, have you measured the altitudes at those points? Or firstly, if I can ask you about Markale Market. Have you measured the altitude at Markale Market?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I have. The altitude is 556 metres above sea level.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And how did you measure that?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Again that was using a GPS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And have you measured the altitude at Sharpstone?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I have. That altitude was 874 metres above sea level with the GPS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And generally speaking, if you were to follow a line north north-east through Markale Market, through Sharpstone and kept going, would the altitude immediately after rise or fall?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: It would rise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's one more issue I wish to address with Mr. Hogan. I wonder whether now's a good time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it is convenient for you, yes. We'll take a break for half an hour and resume at 5 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Before I address the last issue with Mr. Hogan, there are two matters to deal with. The first is the images, the 360-degree images in 65 ter 10419. I'd ask that they be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2213, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And the second, if we could return to 65 ter 21213. You will recall this is the very first photograph we looked at. We now have the panoramic version uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, this is a image we looked at before or looked at part of it before. You said it was taken from the Pale road and you were in the company of Mr. Lesic when he took this photograph. I'll ask you to mark four features on this photograph with the pen. The first one is the state hospital?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Number 1. The second one, marking with number 2 is the Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: The third marking with number 3 is the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And the fourth with number 4 is Markale Market.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I'll have to draw a little arrow to the marketplace. It's very difficult to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And your signature and today's date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And perhaps, Mr. President, this can replace Exhibit 2185.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any objections from Defence? So at that will be done. That -- Exhibit P2185.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, do you know who Colonel Andrej Demurenko is?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: He was a witness in the trial of Dragomir Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And just briefly, in what capacity do you know him, i.e., what was his position at the relevant time period that he testified about?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: In August of 1995, he was a Colonel in the Russian army, seconded to UNPROFOR. He was the Chief of Staff to the commander of Sector Sarajevo, as far as I can recollect.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with his view as to why the Bosnian Serbs could not have been responsible for the shelling of Markale Market at the end of August 1995?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And if you could briefly describe the view or theory as you understand it.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: During his testimony in the Defence case for Dragomir Milosevic, Colonel Demurenko produced a -- or showed a video and testified that the investigation conducted by both UNPROFOR and the local Bosnian investigators revealed the angle at which the 120-millimetre mortar impacted the street in front of the market building and the direction of fire of that mortar. Using a mortar table for an M-52 mortar, Colonel Demurenko, in the video and in his testimony, worked out the six possible points at which that mortar could have been fired. He testified, and he stated on the -- in the video that he physically attended, along with VRS soldiers, the three possible sites on the VRS side of the confrontation lines and viewed the ground within a 10-metre radius of those sites and found no signs of a mortar having been fired. Therefore, he said that if it did not come from those three particular sites within 10-metre radius, it could not have originated from the VRS side.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Have you ever been asked to conduct an investigation to test part of this view?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I was, in the summer of 2007 I was so tasked.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe what you did in order to test part of that theory or view?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Because Colonel Demurenko had stated on the video that he used a direction of fire of 176 degrees and distances of possible points of origin of -- I believe it was 3.600 metres, 3.400 metres, and 2.700 metres, I believe, or 2.400 metres, I'm not sure, but I got the assistance of our mapping unit to produce a satellite image of the area of Sarajevo with markings of 176 degrees from Markale Market and little arrows to indicate the distances at which Colonel Demurenko had stated those possible launch sites. I also had them mark a line of 170 degrees, because 170 degrees was the indication in the UNPROFOR report of the direction of fire. I then attended Mount Trebevic and tried to go as closely as possible to those possible launch sites, those potential launch sites to take GPS readings and to take photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: 65 ter 23085, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I believe that what we're about to see is a series of photographs that you took whilst on that mission, as you've just described. Firstly, what will come up on our screens is an attachment to those photographs, an index of those photographs, and I'd ask you to confirm, Mr. Hogan, that the information recorded here reflects the information you recorded with your GPS on Mount Trebevic and that you logged with the evidence unit upon return?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Before looking at those photographs I want to go to 10417. 65 ter 10417, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned before that prior to going on the mission you worked with the mapping unit using a satellite image, and you marked out 170 degrees and 176 degrees, and you marked the different waypoints where the photographs were taken. Does this image reflect that exercise?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Now, I'll first ask this image to be admitted into evidence unmarked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2214, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And just for the benefit of the Court now, can you circle waypoint 2, 3, and 5 on that map.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]. I should point out that there's actually a small black crescent which can be visible beside the letters WP and the number, and that small crescent Is the actual spot THAT I was standing on when taking the GPS reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I don't think we need to admit this marked version. The -- as Mr. Hogan has explained by referring to that small black crescent, the image is self-explanatory. If we can go back to 23085, the series of photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know where this is. Could it please be marked. I don't see what you mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, if we zoom in further. Let's zoom in the bottom part where we can see "WP2."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Turn to page 10, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Now, according to the information at the beginning of this series of photographs, this is a photo taken at waypoint 2. Can you confirm that's the case?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Turn to page 12, please. Again an image taken at waypoint 2; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And final image, waypoint 2 is page 15, according to the information in the index. Thank you. Now turning to page 21. We might go to the next image, sorry. Page 22, then. And now look at page 24 -- sorry, page 25. Page 25, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And can you confirm those three images we've just seen, the GPS reader and those two photographs, were taken at waypoint 3?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And we'll finally go to page 40, and to page 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Can you confirm that these two images we've just seen were taken at waypoint 5?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender the series of photographs, the full series of photographs along with the index at the front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2215, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hogan. That concludes the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. It's now for you to cross-examine Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I hope that you will understand that since our time is very short, I will try to put questions that will make it possible to give a mere yes or no answer. Sometimes I understand that you will have to say more than that. What was -- what was your task in terms of finding the locations of these incidents?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: My task was to find -- are you talking about the photographs on Trebevic or the sniping and shelling incident locations?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All locations. Your overall task. When you were given this task, what was it that your task was? What were you supposed to establish in relation to all the incidents or all the locations that you visited?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Regarding the shelling and sniping locations, my task was to find out -- to accompany the witness or the victim to the location to establish as closely as possible where the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you had the assistance of the witness. Was that the crucial point, when the witness would say where a particular incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: That's what I was using as my guidebook, yes. Where the witness said the incident happened, that's what I took as the incident location.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have the assistance of witnesses in terms of places where fire had come from?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Regarding sniping incidents, they could indicate the direction of fire, but by the very nature of being hit by a bullet, they were not in a position to say exactly what the precise origin of fire was. They knew where -- which direction the bullet came from, but they did not know precisely which building or feature that bullet originated from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you use the results of the official investigation of the local police with the assistance of the witnesses, or did you simply restrict yourself to where the witnesses would take you to?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify the procedure I was taking, I was not -- I was not gathering their evidence at that point. I was only taking them to -- having them take me to the locations for the purposes of this filming. When they came to testify, that was the important part of identifying the sources of fire. At the time that we were doing the filming, I only asked for the direction of fire. So we did not use the statements or the police investigation reports or the UNPROFOR reports at the time of these filming incidents -- these filming procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, this fire is determining the location is concerned, in addition to being taken to different places by witnesses, did you also have information as to what it was that the local police had established the location to be?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes. The local police investigation reports were tendered into evidence at the trial, yes. I didn't -- I did not consult them for the purposes of the filming. I depended upon the witnesses. This -- this exercise was designed to shorten the witnesses' testimony. It was not to take their evidence at the -- at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we therefore infer that you were not in a position to compare the location of the incident that was established by the local police on the one hand, and on the other hand, what the witness had shown -- or the victim, rather?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: During the filming, no, I did not compare.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you set the coordinates in accordance with what the witnesses had shown you, and that is what is on your films; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When determining the location involved, do you determine the coordinates of the location where you were standing or the location where the incident had taken place?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I would stand at the location where the witness or victim indicated that he or she was hit by the bullet or the person had been killed by the bullet, and that's where I was standing when I took the GPS reading. And I'm speaking of sniping incidents now. The shelling incidents were a little bit different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It seems that you used Garmin GPS or Garmin or whatever the pronunciation may be. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us in the briefest possible terms what the technical capabilities and technical characteristics of that device are?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't. I know how to turn it on, and I know how to take a reading. I don't know how it actually works. It's like a computer. I know how to turn it on and use it, but I don't know how it actually works.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3091. Could we have that, please, in order to get some education in terms of the letters and numbers that this device can display. Yes, that was it. Thank you. That's the device, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, or one very similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you explain to us what the lettering means and what the numbers depict?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: The screen shot of this instrument is set for compass reading, and it indicates that -- that the GPS unit is pointed south at a degrees of 202, and at the bottom is 0.0 speed. So the unit is stationary while this screen shot is taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So it works in compass mode. That's what we see here; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: It can. That's -- that's one of the functions of the unit. It can work in compass mode, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 1D -- actually, let me just ask this: Can we tender all of this together once we're done with all of these photographs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is another photograph, 1D3092. Can that be on one side of the screen and then can it all be admitted together as a single photograph? So 1D3092. Could that be on half of the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us now which mode this is?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: This is operating in a waypoint, for want of a better term. This displays a grid reference where the unit is located at the time of the reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When measuring the coordinates, did you express them in such numbers, such seven-digit numbers?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: No. The -- the readings that I recorded on the attachment to the previous exhibit were in decimal degrees, so degrees with decimal points. You can display the readings in degrees, minutes, seconds; decimal degrees; or with what they call UTM, universal transverse mercator of grid references.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what did you use?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I used decimal degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you use the global coordinate system?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that term.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the term "GWS"?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this photograph be admitted as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Two images will be admitted into one Defence exhibit. So they should be merged as page 1 and page 2 later on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He doesn't have to sign it; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you give the number again, D?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's Exhibit D990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's part of the still from a video. Yes. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, when coordinates are established in the way in which you established them, can they be entered into the maps that were used by UNPROFOR -- or, rather, the coordinates that you establish in this way, are they identical to the coordinates that were established by UNPROFOR when they worked on this?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I have no idea. I'm not sure exactly which maps UNPROFOR was using, and I don't know whether they would be able to be transferred, but if -- logically, if they were using maps that displayed latitude and longitude with enough detail, you could take the latitude and longitude readings from a GPS and mark the appropriate location on a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you did not make these comparisons. You did not establish whether it was compatible with the maps and coordinates use by UNPROFOR; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I did not specifically do that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You do understand why I'm putting these questions. I understand. I'm not criticising you. We have documents and exhibits that come from UNPROFOR, and that's why I'm asking you these questions. All right. You dealt with the incident location at Zmaja od Bosne that occurred on the 8th of October, 1994; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is that one of the F scheduled incidents? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it was that you said here, what it was that you established in relation to this location? Have you heard what you said, or would you like us to play this again?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: No. I was reading the GPS coordinates from the instrument into the camera. That's what I was reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that position pertains to the spot where you are standing; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I don't know. As I said before, I -- I might have gone over to the tram tracks, taken a reading and stored it into the GPS unit, walked back onto the sidewalk and read it off the screen. I'm not sure. Or I could have taken it on the sidewalk. I'm not sure exactly what -- which method I used. I should point out, though, that you can hear me saying the degrees, minutes and seconds for the readings, and then when I returned to The Hague and was providing the readings to mapping unit, they preferred to work with decimal degrees. So instead of saying 49 minutes, 20 -- 49 degrees, 20 minutes, 13 seconds, they preferred 49.xxx degrees, and the instrument can convert those automatically just by adjusting the settings. So that's how I recorded them in my later declaration with the decimal degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is now putting a special task before us. Can we ask for a break of about 10 minutes to establish how we are going to proceed in view of this new fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Until we find our bearings in terms of all this electronics, Mr. Hogan, could you have a look at this map of the US government. Could you look at the markings there, and can you tell us how it reflects on your work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we switch to e-court, then.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then have in e-court 0361-5780. That should be the map. 0361-5780. That's the ERN number. The map should be there. It should be on the ELMO. Thank you. Could you put it lower down and then move it to the left a bit. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at 26 seconds -- or, rather, 94 on a horizontal plane. And the next one is 95 and 27 seconds, and then on the vertical one we have 43, 52, and 55 seconds. What are these markings, and how does that influence the measurements that you were telling us about?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: This map, if you're talking about the letters CC, DD, EE, across the horizontal top -- is that what you're? Okay. 93, 94, 95, those are grid lines, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The numbers.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: And then -- then there are also numbers, 26 minutes, 27 minutes, and those are the -- the degree minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us now what you did and what was converted here? How was that conversion carried out?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I didn't use this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that, but I'm speaking of these minutes, seconds, degrees. Can you explain that to the Trial Chamber? Can you explain what it was that you did and how that was converted here in this -- in which way?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I see. The GPS instrument has a variety of ways to display your location. You can either display it by grid reference with these -- using the numbers 93, 94, 95, across the top, 60, 61, et cetera, along the side. So horizontal and vertical numbers. Where they intersect would give you a one-square kilometre range. By narrowing it down, if you had 9456 by 6178, for example, you could get within 10-square metres using those grid references. However, when I first recorded, as we saw, on that video the position, I was using degrees, minutes, and seconds. So each degree is divided into 60 minutes, and each minute is divided into 60 seconds. That's one alternative display on the GPS. The third alternative is decimals, so you can have decimal degrees. 45 -- for example, 45 degrees, 30 minutes, 0 seconds, equals 45.50 degrees in decimals. So you can display them anyway you want. And taking the same position, you -- just by changing a setting on the GPS unit, it will automatically convert the display. It's the same location, just displayed differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But if it's done here rather than on the spot, what happens?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I couldn't hear you. I couldn't hear the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If that is done here in The Hague rather than on the spot where you were taking measurements, what would you do then? How would you convert it then?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Well, there are very simple computer programmes that will do it automatically. It's -- it's very common measurements. It can be -- I'm sure if you just do an internet search, you can find a very good computer programme that will convert it into whichever reading you want very accurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is there any loss in translation, to put it metaphorically? Is there any loss, any error in this conversion?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: In -- in the conversion from one reading to another, no, there's no -- it's the same. The actual reading, the accuracy depends upon how many satellites you're able to access at the time, whether you're accurate within 30 metres, or accurate within 10 metres, or accurate within 1 metre. It depends on how many satellites are available that you can access. But the actual reading will get you just as precisely to the same location, whether it's in the grid, or degrees, minutes, seconds, or decimal degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you agree it would be useful to us to have both measurements and see for ourselves how the conversion was done.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I'm sure that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Sorry. That's a question really asking for speculation on the part of the witness. He doesn't know what's useful for the Defence or others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't -- I don't think I follow that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, my question is should this be verifiable? Shouldn't we be able to have all the measurements and check for ourselves whether the conversion was done correctly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, Mr. Hayden -- I'm sorry. Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sure that they can be converted very easily. But I must point out that the reason that these GPS readings were taken was for the purpose of putting dots on these maps that have been provided, and the dots themselves are probably a hundred metres in diameter. So to get it accurate within 1 metre I don't think is going to make much difference to the placement of these dots on the maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm just trying to say that if the measurement was done in one system and was represented to us in a different system, I think I should have -- I should be given the chance to check for myself whether the conversion was done correctly. Am I able to check that if I don't have both measurements?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I -- I'm not sure if you can -- as I say, they can be converted very easily with a programme.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: After the break, can you show an example how a specific grid reference is converted into -- I don't know the name, but to be able to mark a specific point on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly. Your Honour, Mr. President, I probably need the assistance of the mapping unit to demonstrate the computer programme that converts it, but I can certainly show how to mark on a map the various grid references and GPS readings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: There's a difference, isn't there, whether you're working from the map to the location or the location to the map, and there will be a difference. If you're seeking to find your position in a completely featureless area, like the middle of the sea, then the accuracy of GPS, according to the number of satellites, will be important but not critical. Especially if you're only travelling at five knots. But if you're looking for a particular location on the ground where you might want to go in for, say, a six-figure grid reference as opposed to a four-figure grid reference to give you the enhanced accuracy that that provides, Dr. Karadzic does have a point. What really matters at the end of the day is were you satisfied with the accuracy of your measurements.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you like me to respond to that, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the purposes of the mapping exercise that I was doing, I was satisfied with the accuracy. As I say, the dots that we were placing on the map were -- convert to about 100 to 150 metres in diameter, and the purpose of these readings and the videos of the witnesses was not to replace their testimony. It was to shorten their testimony. So the important points that were made were while they were testifying and their evidence was being -- was able to be tested during cross-examine. This was only just to demonstrate that the locations -- to shorten their testimony for the Court's purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can just make an observation that some of those victims were not allowed to testify because their testimony was admitted under Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, you would agree, wouldn't you, that in the circumstances of street fighting, when the confrontation line sometimes bisects a building, these deviations of 100, 150 metres make a big difference. And we've had experience with mapping by UNPROFOR where the error margin was 300 metres. Do you agree that we have good reason to want to protect ourselves from these errors?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I would agree that you have reason to protect yourself from errors, but I must stress that the reason that these GPS readings and dots were placed was not to prove the -- the elements of each incident. It was to assist in shortening the testimony of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at e-court and go back to that place where you established the coordinates for this incident from October 1994 in Zmaja od Bosne Street.

utterances.text: Witness -- could we see that film again. I think she was standing much further to the west, and we can establish that, because this is oriented to the south. So the west is on the left side.

utterances.text: I note the time, Mr. Karadzic. Shall we take a break or -- yes. We'll have a break for half an hour, so we'll resume at 1.00.

utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. May I --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- just address you very briefly on one matter, and that is, we would like to make a motion for reconsideration of the Chamber's oral decision of the 1st of February that denied Dr. Subotic anything in the way of consideration for other than to be physically present in the courtroom concerning the testimony of this witness. We, as you suggested, contacted OLAD, and they have refused to compensate her, saying that the Trial Chamber made it clear that Dr. Subotic is not required to provide expert assistance to Dr. Karadzic and, rather, allowed her presence in the court to assist Dr. Karadzic exceptionally instead of another team member. And I think that you can see from the quality of the examination that has been -- the cross-examination that has been done, that the assistance of an expert was indeed required for this witness. And we don't think it's fair to require people on the Defence to work pro bono, and Prosecution experts and there's a whole mapping team that's assisting Mr. Hogan, all of whom are being compensated regularly for their work. So we would ask that you reconsider your decision and allow Dr. Subotic to have the same status with this witness as she has had for every other witness in which she's been allowed to participate in the courtroom. Thank you.
