utterances.text: I think it's the same. We'll see in a moment. We see the date 22nd July 1994. Is that when the incident happened, 22nd --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic is referring to the B/C/S version, second line, but we must have a translation for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, here's the translation: "[In English] Photo 5. Reference: Sniper wounds. Place: Sarajevo, Miljenka Cvitkovica Street 4. Date of photo --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it's photo file. Place: Sarajevo, Miljenka Cvitkovica Street 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps if I could see the next page. I'm not sure which incident this reference is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know this cafe?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I've been to that cafe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the traces -- the evidence was led about this incident based on the traces of damage on this cafe, and that's in that documentation.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: There was damage on that cafe, and I believe there was damage on the window of the -- the shoe store, which is just to the right of the edge of this photograph, on the other side of the passageway that's visible. And, of course, there was damage on the young boy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that this cafe is located in a completely different street, Dzemal Bijedic Street, which never changed its name?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the name of the street at the time, but this is the cafe, that's the passageway, and just off the edge of the photograph is the shoe store where this incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the shoe shop is in a completely different street that was called once Miljenka Cvitkovica and now it's called Ferde Hauptmana, and this cafe is in a completely different street on the opposite side of the block?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we show the witness the next page of this document, both in B/C/S and English. Is this the one you refer to as the shoe shop?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We need a redaction of that last answer, and although it hasn't been tendered for admission, if it is, the video does need to go under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The problem, Mr. Hogan, is the fact that the Street of Dzemala Bijedica did not change its name, and it's not Miljenka Cvitkovica. Perhaps the incident did occur in the Miljenka Cvitkovica, but it was investigated in the street of Dzemala Bijedica.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Well, I have no control over what the investigator at the time wrote down for a street address, but this is the location. Whatever the street address was, this is the location that's depicted in the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, what we displayed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It has already been admitted as P19.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The previous one, the video we showed, 1D3110.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll admit it under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1003, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have to hurry. Let us move on to F7 in this case. It's the 25th of May, 1995. You were taken there as well. So could the distinguished Mr. Hayden tell us whether we can have this broadcast, whether this is a protected witness. Incident F7.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. I'm -- I'm unable to make that determination without seeing who is on that video, so please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, let's not broadcast this video.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have played 1D3111 from 58:09 up until 1:02:08.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "Would you please show me by standing at the location where the front of the bus was located at the time it was hit by a bullet, to the best of your recollection. "I will now mark this line with yellow paint. "Could you please show me where the side of the bus was. "I will now mark that line with yellow paint. "Could you please show me by standing on the location where, to the best of your recollection, you were located at the time the bus was hit by a bullet. "[Indiscernible] "I will now mark that with a figure X and a number 1. "Could you please show me by standing on the spot where, to the best of your recollection, the bullet hit the side of the bus. "I will now mark this spot with X and the number 2. "To the best of your recollection, can you show me where passenger A was seated. "[Interpretation] Here. "Thank you. I will place a number 3 beside this location. "Could you please show me, to the best of your recollection, where passenger B was located. "I will mark this spot with an X and a number 4. "Could you please indicate by pointing which direction the bus was facing. "Could you please indicate by pointing from which direction, to the best of your recollection, you heard the gunshot at or near the time that the bus was impacted by the bullet. "And finally, could you please show me where the back of the bus was located to the best of your recollection."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you help us with this: Can you tell us what the orientation would be in terms of cardinal points over here?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: The -- this is -- this is in Dobrinja. The front of the bus, as indicated by the witness, would have been facing south-west, I believe, and the camera right now is facing south-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The camera that is filming this, not the one that can be seen in the background; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Correct. The one that can be seen in the background would be facing north-west. I'm sorry, I'm not sure what I just answered for the camera that we're looking from. The camera angle that's being shown now is facing south-east, and the one that's -- that's in the background is facing north-west.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This witness is indicating that the bullet had come from the north-west; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes. From the direction of Nedzarici, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are going to establish whether it was actually from Nedzarici, but the important thing is that it's north-west. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: It may be a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Exhibit D1004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: "This is shelling incident number 1. "Once again, could you please stand on the spot --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you please stop it. Yes, Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt the video-clip. I can raise this afterwards but I just wanted to note, looking at the time, that I do have around five minutes of re-direct examination. I didn't want to run out of time at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have a separate fixed witness for the next week. Is my understanding correct, Mr. Tieger? How much longer would you need for this witness, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would need another hour, but I'll try to fit into the time that you have given me. If we could go on a few minutes after 2.30, that would be useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If -- if you would be able to finish your cross-examination till -- we'll give additional 15 minutes, we'll do that, but otherwise, we may think about interposing this witness with the next witness, given that Mr. Hogan is working here. So there should be no difficulty in calling him again if necessary. So I leave it in your hands, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll do my best to finish. If necessary, we're going to ask for him to come and testify again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, you have also been shown this incident G4, rather, the location of incident G4 from this case, and that is a question -- no. Actually, it is shelling. The shelling of a playground; right? 1D3112. That's it; right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this played.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "Show me by standing on the spot where, to the best of your recollection, the second shell exploded on the 1st of June, 1993."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did this witness show you the location -- or, rather, the damage that was sustained and this red mass?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: What he was showing me was a -- was a crater created by a shell that had been preserved by pouring in red-coloured cement-type or asphalt-type sealant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to this film, you were shown the location where the second shell fell, the second one in that incident; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: In -- in this film clip, yes. In previous -- if you had seen previously, he would have shown the first shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please confirm that the witness indicated to you the direction from which he heard the shot?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I don't recall. I don't recall. I'd have to watch the whole film clip. I just don't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that tempore criminis, that is to say, at the time of the incident -- or, rather, in November 1995, when an investigation was carried out after the incident, that the local police established that the second shell fell on the soil and that there were no traces of the second shell on the asphalt. The second one fell into a field, a garden, whereas the first one fell on asphalt.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I know that that's what the investigation report said of their efforts two and a half years after this incident happened, but this witness lives in the area. He was there at the time. I think I'll go with what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So this witness showed you two craters on an asphalt surface; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In 2001; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I believe -- yes, it was 2001 we filmed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The incident took place on the 1st of June, 1993. The investigation was carried out in November 1995, and it was established then that there is one crater on the asphalt and that the second shell fell into soft soil that was covered with some vegetation and the crater could not have been examined at all. Do you see that there is something wrong there?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I see the discrepancy, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Also, this investigation in 1995 was carried out in the presence of representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor. So a representative of the OTP was there when it was established that there is one crater on the asphalt surface.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer, Mr. Witness. Mr. Hayden, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I believe it's on our 65 ter list, maybe already admitted as an exhibit, but could we have a reference for this investigation of 1995 so we can make sure we're all referring to the same document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can tell you the 65 ter number. 09970, page 4 in Serbian. It is the local investigation. In English it is page 5. The number is the same. And the number of the investigation -- I don't know the exact number of the Prosecution. It's probably the same number, but the English and Serbian are 0 -- 65 ter 09970. The Serbian version page 4, the English page 5. That was the representative of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1699, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit 1699?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1699, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If necessary, let's. Let us see perhaps see this page in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Excellency, the first investigation in 1995 was carried out two and a half years after the incident had occurred and there were not two craters then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question to the witness is whether he is aware of the fact that he had been misinformed -- or, rather, that they did not show him what the actual situation was, namely that there was a significant discrepancy. That has been confirmed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did answer that I -- I see the discrepancy, but I don't believe I was deliberately misled by this witness that we're seeing on the film. He's showing me what to the best of his recollection and knowledge actually happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to accuse this witness, but it is a fact that in 1995 there were not two craters there. Otherwise they would have been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Don't you agree that the right thing to do would have been to carry out the investigation on the 1st and 2nd of June, 1993, that that would have been a proper investigation?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I do believe that there were -- there were efforts to do so, in fact, by the UN commission of experts that were in Sarajevo, but they were unable to get to Dobrinja because of the danger and there was ongoing shell-fire, and they could not safely attend that scene to do the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has this been admitted? Is this video part of some exhibit? 1D31112. The one that we showed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1005, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said and you confirmed today and I think that's contained in the statement as well that it was your task to collect inculpatory and exculpatory material during this expedition of yours. Did you collect any exculpatory evidence?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are we going to get that?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I do believe that there has been a lot of disclosure under Rule 68 made to you. It was made to Stanislav Galic -- sorry, to Dragomir Milosevic in that case, and I do believe it's been disclosed to you as well under Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they inform you about the deployment of forces? Were you aware of the fact that this was urban warfare, the front line went through the streets, actually through buildings themselves?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I know that there were portions of the front line that did go through city streets, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did they inform you during that tour of yours about the deployment of forces? Do you know, for example, who was at Grdonj and who was at Hum? These two hills are impressive, and you remembered them.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I'm not sure which tour you're talking about, but during my investigation and my involvement in the various Sarajevo cases, I do know that Hum and Grdonj were within the ABiH lines, although they're -- that's -- that's a broad way to say -- of saying it regarding Grdonj because -- for various reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I meant your stay, that one-week stay. I'm not underestimating it in any way, or its importance, this investigation, this one-week-long investigation. Do you know about the other positions in town, who was deployed where?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: In general terms, but I would probably have to refer to a map for more -- to be able to answer precisely for positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I received interpretation today that you said that Colonel Demurenko had been loaned to UNPROFOR. Was he part of UNPROFOR just like all other officers were belonging to different nationalities?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know if that word "loaned" is accurate. It's seconded or assigned to UNPROFOR. His status was the same as all other UNPROFOR officers, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what Colonel Demurenko's position was in the Sarajevo command?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I believe he was the Chief of Staff of Sector Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that you said today that Demurenko used M-52 tables?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: That's what he showed on the video which was used in -- by the Defence in the Dragomir Milosevic case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have information that he used TG120 M-75 tables. So we are going to collate that. All right. Tell us now, on pages 37 and 38 in P2214, you -- actually, can we have that, P2114. Is it correct that you were sent to locations that are on the northern slopes of Trebevic, that is to say, those slopes of Trebevic that are facing the city itself?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that they were trying to justify the fact that they did not see the shells was due to the fact, as they say, that they were fired from the southern slope of the hill? Did anybody tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Who are you saying "they"? I'm not sure who you're referring to. They didn't see the shell, or they didn't know, or they told. Who's "they"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: OP 1, I think. I think that is observation point 1 below this trajectory that you drew. They said that they did not hear or see any shells, and the justification was that the shell had been fired from the other side of Trebevic, from behind the mountain. But all right. You don't really have to deal with that? Did you choose these locations?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I can answer that if you wish. The fact is that OP 1 was on the slopes of Colina Kapa, which has rising ground behind it to the north of it. So Trebevic is largely shadowed by the slopes of Colina Kapa. That's why -- it wasn't suggested that the mortar was fired from the southern slopes of Trebevic. It was suggested that it was fired on the other side of Colina Kapa, which would be the north slopes of Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, did you choose these locations, or did somebody suggest them to you?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Colonel Demurenko chose these locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know at what angle of descent shells fall from these locations? What angles would that have to be? Let me better ask you: Do you know where the front line runs through here?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: At the time it was along the Pale road, which would be -- I mean, I can mark it if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that and tell us who controlled Colina Kapa at the time.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]. And Colina Kapa was in ABiH territory at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that between the front line and Markale there is at least 2.5 -- 2.5 kilometres, if not even more than that?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: No. You can see on this -- on this satellite photo the 2.000-metre mark is already on the slopes of Trebevic, south of the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But there was no less than 1.500 metres, according to your map; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Right. From the front line to Markale about -- yes, about 15, 1.600 metres, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put the date and the signature, please.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1006, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we didn't admit the video-clip that was played, which is 1D3099, on the ground that it has been already admitted, but I was advised it was not admitted, so we will admit it. Relevant transcript page number is page 66, lines 10 to 13. So we will give a separate number for this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit D1007, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, if you are able to conclude in ten minutes' time, we'll continue, but otherwise -- yes, you can? Let's do that, then.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can. I'll do my best. Could we now take a look at 65 ter 10419 -- or, rather, it's P2209. Exhibited today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please tell us --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You marked this today. Were you informed that the shots came from the location that is marked here, from that direction?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I don't recall. This incident is one of the tram sniping incidents, and I don't recall what the evidence was as per the direction or source of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked earlier today to mark high-rises on Grbavica, and that's when you put this marking; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see I think it's 210 -- P2210. I think I've got it wrong. We can't see much here. Perhaps we should try that part that relates to Spicasta Stijena, Sharpstone, F17. 2211.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, to the best of your knowledge, is it easy for a sniper to target a moving streetcar, a tram, in motion? Would the sight on the sniper rifle compensate for the movement or would it be difficult?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Well, we have had evidence from a sniping expert, but as somebody who has used firearms in the past, I would say it would be extremely easy to target at that moving tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mean to say that the movement of the target does not create great optical distortion and instability. Does it provide for great instability or not?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: If your object is to hit the tram, it is a huge target, and I don't think there'd be any difficulty hitting it with either telescopic sights, open sights, machine-gun. It would not be a difficult target.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know the distance between Sharpstone and the Sedrenik Street? Is this Sedrenik Street that you marked?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: This is Sedrenik Street. I don't recall. I was with the expert when he took measurements from all these locations. I just don't recall what numbers he obtained and included in his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one more question. Do you recall that earlier today you marked Pofalici on a photograph at the request of Mr. Hayden?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know whose neighbourhood it is? Is it a Serb or a Muslim neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I think it's mixed, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that it was controlled by the Muslim army during the war?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Well, everything within the cease-fire -- the confrontation lines in Sarajevo was controlled by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so it does not surprise me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did anyone inform you that already by 15 May 1992, all the Serbs in Pofalici were killed and their houses destroyed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not for the witness to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not asking whether it was a fact. I'm just asking the witness if he had been informed about that. He was an investigator, after all, so he could answer whether he got that information or not. Anyway, thank you, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you can ask the question, but I doubt the necessity of it. Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, during Mr. Karadzic's cross-examination some time was spent on incident F12, which relates to Dzenana Sokolovic and her son, and there was discussion about the location, this precise location of the victims when they were shot. My first question is: Generally speaking, when you went to these locations with the witnesses, did you give them their statements to refresh their memories prior to asking them to mark the locations?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: No. They did not refer to statements or other documents that we had in our possession with the OTP. They were relying solely upon their own memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: And did you -- for example, if there was a relevant video of the incident or the aftermath of the incident, was it shown to them?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: I ask to go to Sanction and ask Mr. Reid to play 65 ter 40110. This is a very -- relatively short clip of about 50 seconds. I'll ask to play it through and then go back to two places in this clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Sorry, we can stop the clip there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: First, Mr. Hogan, do you recognise anyone in this clip?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I recognise the body of young Nermin Sokolovic. He was the victim, and I have seen photos of the rescue personnel before, but I do not recognise anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Is -- and I believe it was Dzenana Sokolovic who was in the clip with you that Mr. Karadzic played the footage. Do you see her in this footage?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I don't recognise her. If she's in this footage, I really don't recognise her.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: If we can go back to the 28-second mark and pause it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Now, do you see where the victim is lying here? Can you describe the road that the victim is lying upon? Do you see, for example, the white markings underneath the victim?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes. This appears to be a cross-walk across the street, a pedestrian crosswalk.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: If I can admit this clip, the 50 seconds we've just played now, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2216, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I was advised that we omitted admitting one video-clip during the Defence examination, which is 1D3100. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1008, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: That concludes the direct examination. I notice that the video-clip we played was played without sound. It is the intention to have it admitted with the sound. There is a soundtrack to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see any problem admitting with sound. Then that concludes your evidence, Mr. Hogan. Thank you for coming. There's one matter --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I -- just one question. Has the whole clip that has been played been admitted? Are we now able to use all of it? Have we admitted the clip or just the still?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have admitted the clip that has been played. Thank you. Now you're free to go, but in the meantime, we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's about Mr. Zecevic, Mr. Tieger. Rather than send a letter to -- as requested by the Prosecution, the Chamber deemed it to be more efficient to ask the VWS to call the witness and convey certain information to him, as well as explore the possibility of his testifying as a Chamber witness. The VWS has reported the result of that conversation to the Chamber, and it is clear that the witness is not willing to testify as a Chamber witness. Therefore, the Chamber would like to ask the Prosecution whether they now wish to request that an order in lieu of indictment and warrant of arrest be issued for the witness or whether they consider that there's another course of action to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, obviously, Your Honour, we would prefer another course if one could be identified. I don't see one under the circumstances. Perhaps not withstanding the Court's explanation about the feedback following VWS contact, we might identify some additional option if we had a brief conversation with VWS. We'd be prepared to do that for the sole purpose of considering any possibilities that we -- we didn't, but otherwise, I think it's clear that the warrant will have to issue. So I would say we should move forward on that unless the Court hears otherwise from the Prosecution through your Legal Officer by the end of this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We are looking forward to hearing from you. The hearing is now adjourned, and I thank you -- we go back to open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I appreciate very much the indulgence of the staff. Have a nice weekend and we will resume on Tuesday at 9.00.
